events.extended_summary: A Houthi missile struck the Al-Aqiq commercial tower housing Aramco offices in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, causing structural damage to upper floors. Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles fired toward the capital. The Houthis claimed responsibility for six military operations targeting Aramco facilities and King Khalid International Airport. The building sustained minor damage from falling shrapnel with no injuries, though witnesses saw ambulances heading to the area. The attack marks an escalation in the war between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis. The Houthis are thought to have demanded $51 billion from Saudi Arabia to end the war, a claim denied by the kingdom. Recent weeks have seen attacks on Riyadh airport, including one that killed 13 people last month.
events.micro_summary: A Houthi missile struck an Aramco building in Riyadh's financial district while Saudi forces intercepted two ballistic missiles.
events.summary: A Houthi missile struck an Aramco building in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, damaging the Al-Aqiq tower, while Saudi air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles. The Houthis claimed responsibility for multiple attacks on Saudi targets.

events.extended_summary: President Isaac Herzog selected former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections. Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, has 28 days to cobble together a coalition and may seek a 14-day extension. Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu commands the 61-seat majority required in Israel's 120-member Knesset. Eisenkot's potential coalition includes his Yashar party, the centre-left Democrats, Naftali Bennett's Together party and Avigdor Lieberman's Yisrael Beiteinu, totaling 48 seats. Arab-led parties Ra'am and the Joint List, holding 19 seats, have endorsed Eisenkot, which would give the anti-Netanyahu camp 67 seats, but Eisenkot has ruled out including Arab parties in his government while Lieberman rejects relying on their support for a minority administration.
events.micro_summary: Gadi Eisenkot has 28 days to form a government after Netanyahu lost his parliamentary majority.
events.summary: President Isaac Herzog tasked opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition lost its majority. Eisenkot has 28 days to assemble a coalition in the 120-seat Knesset where no party holds 61 seats.

events.extended_summary: New Zealand voters face weeks of uncertainty after a knife-edge election left Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's conservative National-led coalition with a paper-thin majority. Preliminary results show the right-wing coalition holding 67 seats in an expanded 131-seat parliament, while the opposition bloc of Labour, the Greens and Te Pāti Māori is projected to have 57 seats. Nearly 400,000 special votes, including those from overseas voters, remain uncounted, meaning final tally could shift the balance of power. The Electoral Commission will deliver official results on November 27, after which coalition negotiations could extend for weeks. The result reflects voter discontent, with the two major parties recording their lowest combined party vote ever at 58%, as swing voters shifted to minor parties. The centrist Opportunity party crossed the 5% threshold to enter parliament for the first time in three decades and may become a kingmaker if the coalition falls short of a majority.
events.micro_summary: New Zealand election leaves conservative coalition with 67 seats and razor-thin majority pending final count on November 27.
events.summary: New Zealand's election left Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's National-led coalition with a paper-thin 67-seat majority in the 131-seat parliament, while the opposition bloc holds 57 seats, with nearly 400,000 special votes uncounted before final results on November 27.

events.extended_summary: On day 1,719 of the conflict, Russia launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, including KN-23 missiles supplied by North Korea, striking 12 Ukrainian regions with Kyiv hit hardest. The attacks plunged five regions into darkness, damaged a kindergarten, residential buildings and the North Bridge, and injured nine people including one child. Energy infrastructure including substations connecting nuclear plants to Kyiv were damaged, disrupting electricity, water and heating as temperatures dropped. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of intensifying strikes to pressure Kyiv ahead of US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday, stating Moscow perceives diplomacy as aggression. Zelenskyy also urged the United States to supply additional Patriot missile interceptors to address shortages.
events.micro_summary: Russia launched 172 drones and 36 missiles at Ukraine, plunging five regions into darkness ahead of peace talks.
events.summary: Russia launched 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles at Ukraine, damaging energy infrastructure and plunging five regions into darkness, injuring nine people, as Kyiv accused Moscow of pressuring it ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

events.extended_summary: President Donald Trump announced on social media that he had offered UFC boss Dana White the position of White House press secretary, calling him 'a violent Fighter and Warrior' who would be a press secretary 'like none other.' Trump urged White to accept and suggested bringing UFC fighters to 'defend us against the Lunatic Left.' White said he is flying to Washington to meet Trump on Monday but declined to say if he was interested, noting he already has many jobs including UFC, Power Slap, Zuffa Boxing, and Meta. White also posted a photo behind the White House press briefing room lectern captioned 'On to the next chapter.' The position has been vacant since mid-October when Katie Zacharia quit after less than five days.
events.micro_summary: President Trump offered UFC boss Dana White the White House press secretary position and will meet him Monday.
events.summary: President Trump offered UFC boss Dana White the White House press secretary job, calling him a 'violent Fighter and Warrior.' White said he is flying to Washington to meet Trump Monday but noted he has many jobs.

events.extended_summary: The Cumbre Vieja volcano on La Palma in Spain's Canary Islands poses a potential megatsunami threat if its western flank collapses into the North Atlantic. Volcanologist Professor Bill McGuire warns that such a collapse could generate 65-foot waves capable of reaching the US East Coast within nine hours, devastating coastal communities. The disaster would also wipe out parts of Europe including La Palma and neighboring islands with waves potentially hundreds of meters high. Computer simulations support these projections, while boulders found in the Bahamas suggest ancient Canary Islands tsunamis crossed the Atlantic. Although not an imminent threat and potentially centuries away, the volcano last erupted in 2021 for 85 days, destroying over 2,800 buildings across nearly 12 square kilometers.
events.micro_summary: Cumbre Vieja volcano collapse could trigger 65-foot megatsunami reaching US East Coast within nine hours.
events.summary: A collapse of the Cumbre Vieja volcano on La Palma could unleash a megatsunami with 65-foot waves reaching the US East Coast within nine hours, devastating coastal communities and parts of Europe.

events.extended_summary: Iran is undertaking significant new construction near at least two major missile sites and repairing bases damaged by months of US and Israeli air strikes. Satellite imagery from November shows digging and new buildings at the Garmdareh military base in Karaj near Tehran and the Shahroud base in the north, while at least 12 other military sites show signs of repairs. New roofs have been built at the Kermanshah missile base, and debris has been cleared at the Parchin military complex. The Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps has transferred missile and drone production lines to underground facilities, allowing continued production while adversaries assumed stockpiles were dwindling. An underground missile city is set to be unveiled, and excavations near Shahroud may be related to moving production underground to protect it from further strikes. Restrictions on missile range have been lifted.
events.micro_summary: Iran constructs underground missile facilities at sites damaged by US and Israeli air strikes.
events.summary: Iran is undertaking significant construction at multiple missile sites, including Garmdareh and Shahroud, building underground facilities to protect missile production from air strikes, while repairing damage from months of US and Israeli attacks at bases including Kermanshah and Parchin.

events.extended_summary: Liverpool secured a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park, halting a two-game losing run and propelling the side back into the top four, nine points behind leaders Arsenal. Florian Wirtz scored his first Premier League goal of the season, assisted by Bradley Barcola, while Alexander Isak added a late goal in the 90th minute to seal the win; Isak now has seven league goals, placing him second in the golden boot race. The result leaves Crystal Palace bottom of the table after 10 games with only two wins, increasing pressure on manager Pierre Sage. Mac Allister tested goalkeeper Dean Henderson within 20 seconds, and Palace, who have scored just nine goals this season, failed to capitalize on first-half chances before Liverpool's second goal just after halftime.
events.micro_summary: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park to end their two-game losing run.
events.summary: Liverpool defeated Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park, ending a two-game losing run and returning to the top four. Florian Wirtz scored his first Premier League goal of the season.

events.extended_summary: Ben Earl (left) and Harry Wilson (right) will meet in England v Australia this weekend England and Australia are set to resume their storied rivalry this weekend, as both sides seek to land a sucker punch in the Nations Championship opener on Sunday. This feels a pivotal Test for both sides, as they look to show their recent improvements are no flash in the pan. England come into the upcoming block finally back to winning ways, after two victories against Fiji and Argentina, but before that had endured their worst-ever Six Nations campaign and lost to the Springboks in their July Nations Championship opener. The Wallabies, meanwhile, seem to have found a new lease of life under new boss Les Kiss, and they sit on a record of five wins from seven in his tenure. However, those two defeats have come in their most recent outings, falling to an aggregate

events.extended_summary: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has stated that Manchester United currently operate at the same elite level as La Liga champions Barcelona ahead of Sunday's Premier League fixture at Old Trafford. Villa travel to Manchester on a five-game unbeaten run but are reeling from a comprehensive 3-0 Champions League defeat against Barcelona. Despite United enduring a dismal domestic campaign under Michael Carrick with just one league victory since August, Emery refuses to underestimate the hosts. The Spaniard has never won at Old Trafford during his managerial career, and Villa have lost their last six visits to the stadium across all competitions. The match represents the final Premier League game before the international break and could be Carrick's last as United head coach, with the club sitting third from bottom in the table.
events.micro_summary: Aston Villa face Manchester United at Old Trafford after suffering a 3-0 defeat to Barcelona.
events.summary: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery compared Manchester United to Barcelona after a 3-0 defeat to them, ahead of Sunday's Old Trafford match where Villa lost their last six visits. United have one league win under Carrick.

events.extended_summary: Usman Khawaja has claimed that the entire Australian cricket team knew about and shared responsibility for the sandpaper ball-tampering scandal during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa. In his memoir Sabr and social media videos, the retired opener said he would "not deny" everyone knew about the plot, though he insisted he had not thrown anyone under the bus. Only captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and opener Cameron Bancroft were suspended and punished for the incident. Khawaja, who retired in January after scoring 6,229 runs in 88 Tests, revealed he had attempted to go public with the details in 2018 and again in 2021. Four bowlers including Pat Cummins, who denied knowledge in a 2021 statement, remain in the team, while former coach Darren Lehmann also denied that everyone knew. Khawaja said Smith, Warner and Bancroft were the victims who took the blame for the whole team.
events.micro_summary: Usman Khawaja claims the entire Australian team knew about 2018 sandpaper use in Cape Town Test.
events.summary: Usman Khawaja claims the entire Australian team knew about and was responsible for using sandpaper on the ball during the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, while only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were punished.

events.extended_summary: Two trains collided between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza, near Cairo, killing at least four people and injuring nearly 90 others. Several carriages derailed after one train struck the rear of another, disrupting railroad traffic. Dozens of ambulances transported the injured to nearby hospitals while cranes were deployed to remove the wreckage. The Egyptian railway system, the oldest in Africa and the Middle East, has a history of deadly accidents, including a fire at Ramses station that killed 25 people and a 2017 collision near Alexandria that killed more than 40. President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the incident with great interest and directed authorities to provide necessary medical care, investigate the circumstances, and hold accountable anyone proven negligent. He also expressed sincere condolences to the families of the deceased and wishes for the recovery of the injured.
events.micro_summary: Two trains collided in Egypt, killing at least four people and injuring nearly 90.
events.summary: Two trains collided between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Giza near Cairo, killing at least four people and injuring nearly 90, with several carriages derailed and dozens of ambulances dispatched to hospitals.

events.extended_summary: A 24-year-old Polish national killed six and injured 17 in a shooting in Kraków's Main Market Square on Saturday, believed inspired by far-right ideologies. Police arrived 23 seconds after the first emergency call and exchanged gunfire with the suspect, who shot at random from his car. Two officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, both under 30, were wounded detaining the gunman. Kulik, a former paratrooper and volunteer firefighter, was hit by three bullets and left critically injured; Morański was shot in the chest. Both underwent surgery and were brought out of medically induced comas on Sunday. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the officers "probably saved many human lives," while Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek stated their response "prevented further human casualties." The suspect remains in critical condition. Police found three bodies at his apartment identified as his parents and sister. A unit specializing in "terrorist offences" is leading the investigation.
events.micro_summary: A gunman killed six in Kraków while two police officers were wounded detaining him, one critically injured by three bullets.
events.summary: A gunman killed six and injured 17 in a Kraków shooting Saturday; two police officers were wounded detaining him, with one critically injured after being hit by three bullets, as officials praised them for preventing further casualties.

events.extended_summary: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck central Japan at 1:04am on Sunday at a depth of 40km in western Shizuoka Prefecture, injuring more than 20 people in Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures. The quake shattered windows, scattered glass across streets, and caused books to fall from shelves. Some injuries occurred when people fell on stairs. The tremor affected a wide area including Hamamatsu, Kyoto, Nara, Yamanashi, and Gifu. No tsunami warning was issued. Authorities warned residents to prepare for possible strong quakes over the next week and to watch for mudslides, falling rocks, and rainfall effects. No changes were detected in the Nankai Trough. Local train services were suspended and Shinkansen bullet trains ran at reduced speeds, with Tokaido Shinkansen services delayed between Shizuoka and Gifu-Hashima stations.
events.micro_summary: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, injuring more than 20 people.

events.summary: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture at 1:04am local time Sunday, injuring over 20 people across Aichi and Shizuoka. The quake shattered windows and disrupted train services, with authorities warning of possible stronger quakes in coming days.

events.extended_summary: Fire largely destroyed Hitler's Eagle's Nest, known as Kehlsteinhaus, on the evening of October 23 at its mountaintop location 1,834 meters above Berchtesgaden in Bavaria. Built by the Nazis in 1938 and frequented by Adolf Hitler, the historic monument had operated as a restaurant attracting tens of thousands of tourists annually. Police arrested a 33-year-old man with a diagnosed mental illness on suspicion of arson and placed him in a secure psychiatric hospital. The blaze has intensified debate over the site's future: some historians advocate clearing the rubble and returning the mountain to its natural state to avoid Neo-Nazi pilgrimage, while Bavarian state officials support rebuilding. The nearby Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, opened in the 1990s, was unaffected. Unlike Hitler's Berghof residence, which was demolished in 1952, the Eagle's Nest survived World War II.
events.micro_summary: Fire largely destroyed Hitler's Eagle's Nest in Bavaria on October 23, sparking a debate over rebuilding.
events.summary: Fire largely destroyed Hitler's Eagle's Nest in Bavaria on October 23. A 33-year-old man was arrested for suspected arson. The site, built in 1938, sparked debate between those wanting it demolished and officials supporting reconstruction.

events.extended_summary: Indian equity markets ended the special one-hour Muhurat trading session on Diwali marginally lower, marking the start of Samvat 2083. The BSE Sensex fell 28.62 points, or 0.04%, to close at 80,999.40 after touching an intraday high of 81,442.11, while the NSE Nifty declined 43.95 points, or 0.18%, to settle at 24,986.40, slipping below the 25,000 mark. The decline ended an eight-year run of gains for both benchmark indices during Diwali sessions and followed a seven-session rally that delivered the strongest weekly gains since February 2021. Despite the fall, investors' wealth increased by Rs 2.60 lakh crore, taking total BSE market capitalisation to Rs 5,05,67,743.40 crore. Seven of 16 sectoral indices ended positive, with pharmaceuticals gaining 1.7% and metals rising 0.4%, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 rose 1% and Midcap 100 gained 0.1%.
events.micro_summary: Indian stock markets ended Diwali Muhurat trading marginally lower, with the Sensex closing at 80,999.40.
events.summary: Indian equity markets ended Sunday's Diwali Muhurat trading session marginally lower after a seven-session rally, with the Sensex falling 0.04% to 80,999.40 and the Nifty declining 0.18% to 24,986.40, ending an eight-year run of gains.

events.extended_summary: India's economic growth is expected to accelerate in the coming year, supported by strong macroeconomic fundamentals and renewed foreign investor interest, Ashishkumar Chauhan, Managing Director and CEO of the National Stock Exchange, said during Muhurat trading on Diwali. India remains the world's fastest-growing major economy with a 7.5 per cent year-on-year GDP growth rate, and Chauhan expressed confidence that momentum would strengthen further. Despite importing nearly 85 per cent of its oil requirements, India is managing its fiscal deficit well through strong tax collections, enabling heavy investment in infrastructure and job creation. Domestic financial savings have grown to nearly USD 1.4 trillion annually, while foreign institutional investors have shown renewed interest in Indian equities ahead of the new Samvat year. The NSE has also achieved nanosecond-level response times, positioning it as the fastest exchange globally, and is deploying artificial intelligence to enhance analytics for retail investors.
events.micro_summary: India's economy is expected to accelerate with 7.5% GDP growth and renewed foreign investment, NSE CEO says.
events.summary: India's economic growth is expected to accelerate in the coming year, backed by 7.5% GDP growth, nearly USD 1.4 trillion in domestic savings, and renewed foreign institutional investor interest, NSE CEO Ashishkumar Chauhan said during Muhurat trading.

events.extended_summary: Foreign portfolio investors invested Rs 38,971 crore in Indian equities this week, reversing earlier selling trends as a sharp decline in global technology stocks made Indian markets more attractive. The shift occurred amid concerns over heavy spending on artificial intelligence and a possible slowdown in data centre investments, which triggered selling across global markets. All three major US indices recorded their biggest single-day losses since April 2025 on Thursday, erasing gains from Wednesday when the Dow jumped more than 1,500 points. While FPIs turned aggressive buyers, domestic institutional investors remained sellers on all trading days. The aggressive buying by FPIs and a short squeeze pushed the Nifty up by 7.58% in a week. India, regarded as a non-AI trade, became a favoured destination due to impressive earnings growth and attractive large-cap valuations.
events.micro_summary: Foreign portfolio investors invested Rs 38,971 crore in Indian equities this week amid global AI stock sell-off.
events.summary: Foreign portfolio investors invested Rs 38,971 crore in Indian equities this week as a global sell-off in AI stocks made India attractive, while domestic institutional investors remained sellers and the Nifty rose 7.58%.

events.extended_summary: Hrithik Roshan attended the 15th LACMA Art + Film Gala at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art on November 7, 2026. The annual fundraising event, co-chaired by Leonardo DiCaprio and Eva Chow since 2011, honoured artist Vija Celmins and filmmaker Denis Villeneuve. Roshan joined international celebrities including Kim Kardashian, Kylie Jenner, Nicole Kidman, Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy, Michelle Yeoh, BLACKPINK's Rosé and AESPA's Ningning. He greeted photographers with folded hands in a traditional namaste and wore a custom-tailored tuxedo with a bow tie. The appearance marked the first time an Indian actor received an invitation to the prestigious gathering, highlighting growing international recognition of Indian film personalities. Proceeds support LACMA's cultural, educational and film programmes.
events.micro_summary: Hrithik Roshan attended the 15th LACMA Art + Film Gala in Los Angeles on November 7, 2026.
events.summary: Hrithik Roshan attended the 15th LACMA Art + Film Gala in Los Angeles on November 7, 2026, joining celebrities including Kim Kardashian and Leonardo DiCaprio, and greeted photographers with a traditional namaste.

events.extended_summary: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part One, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, began its theatrical run on November 5. The film opened with an India net collection of Rs 64.85 crore and a domestic gross of Rs 77.50 crore. On Day 2, collections fell 25.9% to Rs 48.05 crore net. Saturday brought a recovery with Rs 69.80 crore net, pushing the three-day total to Rs 182.70 crore. By Day 4, the film crossed the Rs 200-crore mark, reaching Rs 223.39 crore net with a domestic gross of Rs 266.26 crore. Day 3 Hindi collections contributed Rs 53 crore, followed by Kannada, Telugu and Malayalam. Overseas collections reached Rs 157.25 crore, bringing the worldwide gross to Rs 375.50 crore.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana crossed Rs 200 crore at Indian box office within four days, reaching Rs 223.39 crore net.
events.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana starring Ranbir Kapoor crossed Rs 200 crore at the Indian box office within four days, collecting Rs 223.39 crore net after earning Rs 69.80 crore on Day 3 and Rs 40.69 crore on Day 4.

events.extended_summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated Diwali with security forces at the CoBRA Operations Base in Karanpur, Bastar, Chhattisgarh, describing the occasion as a historic milestone marking the first festival with every district free from Naxalism. He stated that for the first time in 47 years, not a single CRPF personnel member had lost their life while on duty during the past year. Modi expressed gratitude to personnel from the CRPF, CoBRA, BSF, ITBP, SSB and state police forces, conveying the appreciation of 140 crore citizens. He recalled that Left-Wing Extremism had previously affected more than 230 districts across nearly 20 states, with Chhattisgarh witnessing over 1,000 security personnel martyred, including 76 CRPF personnel killed in the 2010 Dantewada attacks. The Prime Minister attributed the achievement to decisive policies adopted after 2014 and the courage of security forces, noting that 50 crore people have also emerged from extreme poverty.
events.micro_summary: Prime Minister Modi celebrated Diwali in Bastar marking first Naxal-free Diwali and no CRPF deaths in 47 years.
events.summary: Prime Minister Modi celebrated Diwali with security forces in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, marking the first Diwali with all districts free from Naxalism and no CRPF deaths in 47 years.

events.extended_summary: Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman called ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina a "convicted criminal" and confirmed Dhaka has requested her extradition from India under bilateral treaty. He said the government would follow due process rather than emotion. The request follows Hasina's November 2025 conviction in absentia by International Crimes Tribunal for crimes against humanity during July-August 2024 uprising, resulting in death sentence on one charge and life imprisonment on another. Hasina fled to India on August 5, 2024, after mass uprising ended her 15-year rule. An interim government led by Muhammad Yunus took charge, and in February Bangladesh Nationalist Party led by Tarique Rahman formed government after parliamentary elections. India has acknowledged receiving extradition requests but has not announced decision, stating matter is being examined through established processes. Hasina has stated she intends to return to Bangladesh in December despite risk of imprisonment or death.
events.micro_summary: Bangladesh requests India extradite ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, convicted and sentenced to death.
events.summary: Bangladesh's Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman called ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina a "convicted criminal" and confirmed Dhaka has requested her extradition from India under the bilateral treaty, following her November 2025 conviction for crimes against humanity.

events.extended_summary: Pakistan Under-19 defeated India by three wickets in the ACC Men's U19 Asia Cup at Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman. Chasing 209, Pakistan found themselves at 63/5 before captain Hamza Zahoor anchored the chase with an unbeaten 100, forming a 107-run partnership with Hasnain Abbas Dar, who scored 38. India had posted 208 in 46.3 overs after a disastrous start that saw captain Lakshya Raichandani dismissed for a duck in the first over. Arjun Rajput scored 107 off 85 balls to give India hope, but the side collapsed to 170/7 before being bowled out. Pakistan's bowlers, led by Ali Raza with three wickets, restricted India, while Zahoor guided his side home with 12 balls to spare. The victory extended Pakistan's winning run against India in the tournament to two consecutive editions and moved them to the top of Group A, with India dropping to second place.
events.micro_summary: Pakistan defeated India by three wickets in the Under-19 Asia Cup, with Hamza Zahoor scoring an unbeaten 100.
events.summary: Pakistan beat India by three wickets in the Under-19 Asia Cup at Al Amerat, Oman, chasing down 209 with Hamza Zahoor's unbeaten 100 after India posted 208, anchored by Arjun Rajput's 107.

Jadeja's fee was revised to Rs 14 crore, down from Rs 18 crore, at which he was retained by CSK ahead of the previous season.

Jadeja wrote, “Happy diwali to everyone” in his Instagram post.

events.extended_summary: Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh became India's 100th chess Grandmaster on Sunday by winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship. The 2004-born player finished with seven points after nine rounds, half a point ahead of Vietnam's Nguyen Duc Hoa, while Nouri Alekhine of the Philippines placed third on six points. Shrivatri, who began the tournament with a loss, won his final two games to secure the title on Diwali, becoming the first Grandmaster from Madhya Pradesh. The milestone ends a wait dating to 1988 when Viswanathan Anand became India's first Grandmaster, following recent additions including S Aswath as the 98th in July and VS Rathanvel as the 99th. Shrivatri earned the International Master title in 2020.
events.micro_summary: Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh became India's 100th chess Grandmaster after winning the ASEAN Plus Open with seven points.
events.summary: Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh became India's 100th chess Grandmaster on Sunday by winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship with seven points, becoming the first Grandmaster from his state.

events.extended_summary: A fire broke out at a factory in the Najafgarh area on Sunday, prompting the immediate deployment of 22 fire service vehicles to the scene. The blaze was reported at 4:21 pm at a factory situated in Nangli Sakrawati, in southwest Delhi. Initially, two water tenders, two water bowsers and a quick response vehicle were rushed to the spot to address the situation. The fire was upgraded to a medium-category blaze at 5:25 pm, following which additional resources were deployed to the factory location in the Najafgarh area. So far, no injuries have been reported in connection with this fire incident.
events.micro_summary: A fire at a Najafgarh factory prompted deployment of 22 fire vehicles with no injuries reported.
events.summary: A fire broke out at a factory in Nangli Sakrawati, southwest Delhi, on Sunday at 4:21 pm, prompting 22 fire service vehicles; the blaze was upgraded to medium-category at 5:25 pm with no injuries reported.
